summary: Screened all 212 atlas roadmap summaries and searched all roadmap documents and 1,968 stage records. Read all 10 Spin stages in full and complete Spin, ClassicalGroups and RootSystems documents, then full candidate stages. Records 16 incoming and 2 outgoing evidence-backed links, plus 6 scoped overlaps. No roadmap-wide merge is proposed. Root-data, group/Lie, integral-carrier and branching interfaces remain explicitly qualified; this is a source-audited link proposal awaiting independent review, not an implementation or a proof that every required theorem exists.

links.reason: For finite-dimensional regular quadratic spaces over fields with 2 invertible, QFI supplies the reflection and Cartan–Dieudonne factorization used by the Clifford conjugation construction. Specialize to C and separately normalize reflecting vectors to prove the complex cover; the general-field spinor-norm image is not replaced by complex surjectivity.

overlaps.detail: Both cover the parity-selected Clifford algebra as a finite-dimensional central simple algebra in the split complex case, but QFI works over general fields and Spin constructs an explicit Fock-model matrix isomorphism. The stronger general-field Brauer assertions do not follow from the complex structure theorem.
overlaps.proposal: Keep general-field central simplicity and Clifford/Brauer invariants in QFI layer 5; keep matrix units and explicit spinor-action isomorphisms in Spin layer 1/4. Reuse Spin layer 0 dimensions and add split-case comparison lemmas, not a second Clifford carrier.

overlaps.detail: The B/D fundamental modules and the first B_l-to-D_l spin restriction meet ClassicalGroups highest weights and its asserted Spin branching/GT boundary. Spin layer 5 specifies Lie-level half-spin identification and a first restriction, not the full group-level Spin(n) branching and normalized GT bases promised by ClassicalGroups layer 6. Half-spin modules also do not descend to SO merely because their Lie algebra is so.
overlaps.proposal: Keep Clifford/spin construction and Lie-level B/D fundamentals in Spin. Keep SO/Sp tensor-built classification and ordinary GT theory in ClassicalGroups. Assign explicit Spin subgroup embeddings, both parity steps of spin branching, group/Lie compatibility and the GT seam to a separate agreed substage; do not insert a false Spin5->ClassicalGroups6 group-branching edge before this contract exists.

overlaps.detail: HighestWeight layer 9 supplies generic reductive/gl_n tools to Spin layer 9, while its CAR worked examples refer back to the Clifford module constructed in Spin layer 9. A reverse edge between the current aggregate stages would create a dependency cycle.
overlaps.proposal: Keep H9->Spin9 for the generic highest-weight/Pieri/isotypic API. Separate HighestWeight CAR acceptance examples from its generic stage: construct the CAR module and its highest-weight computation in Spin9, then consume those in a later application/comparison substage. Do not use the application to prove the generic toolkit.

overlaps.detail: Both specify group-level D4 triality, but ReductiveGroups works with pinned integral Chevalley groups and a tripled carrier, whereas Spin uses a complex Clifford-defined group and trilinear form.
overlaps.proposal: ReductiveGroups owns the pinned automorphism-lifting theorem and integral tripled carrier. Spin owns the pinning-compatible complex Clifford/Chevalley comparison, transport of the automorphism, and spinor/trilinear consequences. Prove that comparison before transferring triality; keep the root-datum order-three map as an explicit upstream request.

overlaps.detail: The full B/D spin modules and their weights appear both in complex spin representation theory and in the CFSG full-weight carrier plan. CFSG needs integral Chevalley-generator matrices, group-scheme faithfulness and positive-characteristic base change, none of which is supplied merely by the complex irreducibility theorem.
overlaps.proposal: Keep Spin complex modules and CFSG/ReductiveGroups integral toral-closure carriers as separate scopes. Share a future integral spin-module/numbering comparison and prove the C specialization agrees; do not infer all-characteristic faithful carriers from complex module dimensions or half-spin irreducibility.

overlaps.detail: Both specify the order-three D4 outer-node permutation. CFSG already fixes it as (0 2 3), fixing Fin index 1; Spin asks RootSystems for the graph symmetry. The combinatorial contract therefore exists in CFSG, but its current aggregate stage also contains finite-field Steinberg maps.
overlaps.proposal: Share the Cartan-matrix permutation and its order-three proof under RootSystems layer 6, then extend it to the simply connected integral root datum. ReductiveGroups layer 9 owns pinned-group lifting. Spin owns complex Clifford transport; CFSG L1 owns Frobenius commutation and twisted fixed-point groups. Do not require the whole positive-characteristic L1 stage as a prerequisite of complex triality.
